stemMd: A species has diploid chromosome number 12. After normal meiosis I, how many chromosomes, each still composed of sister chromatids, are in each daughter cell?
explanationMd: Meiosis I separates homologous chromosomes while sister chromatids remain together. Each daughter receives one chromosome from each of six pairs, so it has six chromosomes, each duplicated.

distractorRationale.b: This incorrectly halves the chromosome number twice.
distractorRationale.a: There are six homologous pairs, not one.
distractorRationale.d: Homologous pairs have separated at the first division.
distractorRationale.e: This confuses replicated chromatids with chromosome count.
